title: Samaṣṭy-abhivādana: salutation to all the deities

words.meaning: to Sandhyā, the goddess of the junction
to Sāvitrī, the verse to Savitṛ as goddess

words.role: the repetition intensifies: ‘salutation again and again’

translation.literal: To Sandhyā salutation. To Sāvitrī salutation. To Gāyatrī salutation. To Sarasvatī salutation. To all the deities salutation, salutation.
translation.readable: Salutation to Sandhyā, to Sāvitrī, to Gāyatrī and to Sarasvatī; to all the deities, salutation again and again.

meaning: After the upasthāna the worshipper turns to the four quarters and salutes four goddesses, one in each, and then all the deities together. Sandhyā is the twilight as a goddess; Gāyatrī, Sāvitrī and Sarasvatī are the forms of the goddess of the Gāyatrī mantra (the evening dhyāna calls her Sarasvatī). The stotrasamhita text marks the directions: Sandhyā east, Sāvitrī south, Gāyatrī west, Sarasvatī north, and all the deities again to the east.
in_the_rite: Step samasti-abhivadana, after the sūryopasthāna, in all three services; followed by kāmo ’kārṣīt and the abhivādana.
